purpose: Quantitative bandwidth comparison of erasure-coded vs full-replication fleet gossip. For each (fleet_size, payload_bytes) cell it reports the real serialized wire cost of the shipped erasure encoder against a full-replication baseline, the fault-tolerance-normalized savings ratio, the metadata-free theoretical ceiling, and a raw dissemination-volume context lens, plus a per-fleet scaling summary and an analytical convergence-vs-bandwidth model.

coding_scheme.description: The measured gossip erasure lane is a systematic XOR single-parity code: it computes exactly one parity chunk (the XOR of all k data chunks) and recovers at most one missing data shard. When the tuned plan allocates more than one parity slot, those extra slots carry identical copies of the single parity chunk and add duplication, not recovery capacity. This is NOT Reed-Solomon over GF(2^8); the report records the real scheme and never fabricates Reed-Solomon polynomial coefficients or the 60-70% savings figure attributed to a tunable Reed-Solomon code. The fault-tolerance-normalized savings ceiling for this single-parity scheme is (k-1)/(2k), which approaches 0.5 (50%) as k grows.

measurement.coding_plan: ErasureCodingPlan::tuned(fleet_size, 0) — the exact plan the live gossip lane derives in encode_evidence_for_erasure_gossip. total_shards (n) = fleet_size; parity_shards ~= n/3; data_shards (k) = n - parity_shards.
measurement.wire_size: Per shard: raw coded payload bytes (shard_payload length) + serialized metadata framing (shard-set id, origin, sequence, index, plan, role, payload length, two content hashes, timestamp, signature, protocol version, extensions), the framing measured by serializing the shard with an emptied payload. The coded payload is counted raw rather than through serde_json (which would expand a Vec<u8> into a JSON number array) so byte totals reflect an on-wire encoding, not a debug serialization.
measurement.full_copy: A full replica is a (1,1) erasure encoding of the whole payload — the same envelope struct — so the comparison isolates chunking and parity from framing.
measurement.determinism: All inputs are fixed (origin node, first sequence, timestamp, shard-set id, generated_at_utc, and a deterministic payload byte pattern p[i] = i mod 251), so the signed report serializes byte-for-byte identically across runs. The gate's deterministic-replay lane compares bandwidth_efficiency_report.json across two runs.

report_fields.scheme_fault_tolerance_erasures: u16; erasures the shipped scheme tolerates per shard set (1)
report_fields.honesty_notes: array<string>; load-bearing disclaimers, including that the scheme is NOT Reed-Solomon and that the ceiling is (k-1)/(2k)
report_fields.methodology: array<string>; how each quantity is measured
report_fields.config: BandwidthComparisonConfig { fleet_sizes: array<u64>, payload_sizes: array<u64>, fanout: u32 }
report_fields.cells: array<bandwidth_cell>; one per (fleet_size, payload_bytes), ordered fleet-major then payload
report_fields.convergence_model: array<convergence_point>; one per fleet_size (analytical, not a live simulation)

bandwidth_cell_fields.data_shards: u16; k, data shards required to reconstruct
bandwidth_cell_fields.total_shards: u16; n, shards emitted by the tuned plan
bandwidth_cell_fields.parity_shards: u16; n - k, identical XOR parity copies
bandwidth_cell_fields.unique_parity_chunks: u16; distinct parity chunks carrying recovery information (1 when parity exists, else 0)
bandwidth_cell_fields.fault_tolerance_erasures: u16; erasures tolerated for this plan (0 or 1)
bandwidth_cell_fields.chunk_len: u64; per-shard chunk length ceil(payload / k)
bandwidth_cell_fields.data_shard_wire_bytes: u64; total wire bytes of the k data shards
bandwidth_cell_fields.parity_shard_wire_bytes: u64; wire bytes of one parity shard (0 when no parity slot)
bandwidth_cell_fields.full_copy_wire_bytes: u64; wire bytes of one full-payload (1,1) copy
bandwidth_cell_fields.shard_metadata_overhead_bytes: u64; framing overhead of a single data shard (wire - chunk_len)
bandwidth_cell_fields.erasure_coded_bytes: u64; PRIMARY lens: k data shards + 1 parity (redundancy to survive one loss)
bandwidth_cell_fields.savings_ratio_millionths: i64; (full_replication_bytes - erasure_coded_bytes) / full_replication_bytes, in millionths; signed (negative when framing overhead dominates)
bandwidth_cell_fields.overhead_exceeds_savings: bool; true when erasure redundancy is at least as costly as replication
bandwidth_cell_fields.theoretical_savings_ceiling_millionths: u64; metadata-free (k-1)/(2k) in millionths; measured savings never exceed this
bandwidth_cell_fields.erasure_as_emitted_bytes: u64; CONTEXT lens (NOT reliability-normalized): total wire bytes of all n emitted shards
bandwidth_cell_fields.full_broadcast_bytes: u64; CONTEXT lens (NOT reliability-normalized): one full copy to every node

scaling_point_fields.data_shards: u16; k for this fleet size
scaling_point_fields.best_payload_bytes: u64; payload with the best measured savings
scaling_point_fields.payloads_overhead_dominated: u64; count of payloads where framing overhead exceeds savings

convergence_point_fields.reference_payload_bytes: u64; largest configured payload, used for the byte columns
convergence_point_fields.analytical_model: bool; always true — an analytical epidemic-push bound, NOT a live network simulation
convergence_point_fields.full_replication_rounds: u64; optimistic epidemic-push rounds to inform the whole fleet
convergence_point_fields.erasure_convergence_rounds: u64; dissemination rounds plus ceil(k / fanout) gather rounds
convergence_point_fields.full_replication_total_bytes: u64; broadcast one full copy to every node
convergence_point_fields.erasure_total_bytes: u64; the erasure lane's emitted shard-set volume

signed_report.report_hash: hex SHA-256 ContentHash over the canonical serialization of report
signed_report.signature_hex: hex signature over the canonical serialization of report

gate.artifacts: bandwidth_efficiency_report.json (signed report; deterministic-replay target), run_manifest.json (outcome=pass, coding_scheme, report_hash), summary.md (per-cell savings table)

tests.unit: crates/franken-engine/src/erasure_bandwidth_accounting.rs #[cfg(test)] mod tests (>=20 cases: config validation, deterministic payload, chunk length, theoretical ceiling closed-form + monotonicity + sub-50%, signed savings math, cell shape for real XOR single-parity, large-payload savings under ceiling, tiny-payload overhead domination, wire-byte consistency, determinism, fleet-of-one degeneracy, empty payload, convergence rounds, report cardinality, no fabricated Reed-Solomon claim, signed report round-trip + hash)
tests.integration: crates/franken-engine/tests/erasure_bandwidth_accounting_integration.rs (>=30 cases: accounting faithful to real encode round-trips across all documented topologies, protocol correctness under coding — reconstruct from data shards, tolerate one loss via parity, reject two losses, identical parity copies, reconstruction receipt scheme, savings ceiling respected, scaling monotonicity, convergence model, report determinism and honesty)
